name: British Columbia short-term rental principal-residence requirement
description: In municipalities of 10,000+ people (and smaller neighbours within 15 km, plus opt-in communities), short-term rentals (under 90 consecutive days) are limited to the host's principal residence plus one secondary suite or ADU; provincial registration required.

attributes.applies_where: municipalities ≥10,000 population plus nearby smaller communities and opt-ins (list as of 1 June 2026 on the page)
attributes.allowed: principal residence + one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit on the same property
attributes.registration: provincial registry; $100/year principal residence, $450/year secondary unit
attributes.exempt: resort municipalities, ski areas, most regional district electoral areas, most Islands Trust areas, hotels/motels, some strata hotels (registration still required)
attributes.local_bylaws: may be stricter (e.g., City of Vancouver business licence)

sources.title: Principal residence requirement for short-term rentals (last updated 21 September 2026)
sources.licence: Province of British Columbia; Copyright and Disclaimer of gov.bc.ca (link and cite; reproduction terms per gov.bc.ca copyright page)

limitations: Effective dates of the requirement and registry not stated on the page. An investment property in Vancouver, Victoria or Kelowna cannot be run as a full-time short-term rental.
